articles.title: Wakefield Trinity make history: How inner sanctum's belief led to first ever Super League semi-final
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity are through to the Super League semi-finals for the first time ever; The Super League Eliminators continue on Saturday October 19 as Warrington Wolves host Hull KR, with kick-off at 5.30pm live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
That inner sanctum, among others, consists of owner Matt Ellis, head of recruitment Ste Mills, and head coach Daryl Powell.

Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.

An example of turning that raw talent into a shining diamond? Caleb Hamlin-Uele. Wakefield saw something in a player who was not breaking through in the NRL. They brought him into the Championship, moulded him, made him one of Super League's best props, and now he is truly in contention to represent England at the World Cup this autumn.

Of course, the biggest success of all would be a trophy. But for now, they are through to their first ever Super League semi-final after their 26-16 victory over Leigh in the Eliminators.

Wakefield's victory was down to their immense forward pack which took control early in the second half. Even with Emre Guler shown red on the hour mark for what appeared to be a punch, they had done enough to keep Leigh at arm's length and see the game home.

It is further reward for what has been a remarkable rise from Wakefield.

"We are going to go where we are going to go. We are just going to prepare as best we can," Powell said.

"Wakefield have never won a play-off game - that is a box ticked.

"Now it is whether we can win a Grand Final. We have two games to do something special.

"You are one game away from getting to a Grand Final that would be huge for the club.

"You have got to be excited by that. We are all excited about how good we can be as a team.

"We will do everything we need to in order to give ourselves the best chance to do that."

Powell has been there and done this before with a team that was not expected to be at the big dance. Castleford, back in 2017, blew everyone away, won the League Leaders' Shield, then beat St Helens with a Luke Gale drop goal to make it to Old Trafford.

They could not complete the final hurdle.

Wakefield have two more hurdles to go. A semi-final against either Wigan Warriors or Leeds Rhinos. A win in that? Then they go to the Theatre of Dreams trying to complete theirs.

If they do that, the inner sanctum's belief that raw potential can become greatness will have been achieved.

Super League play-offs results and schedule

Friday September 18: Wakefield Trinity 26-26 Leigh Leopards

Saturday September 19, Warrington Wolves vs Hull KR, KO 5.30pm on Sky Sports

Semi-Final 1 - Friday September 25, Leeds Rhinos vs TBC, 8pm KO on Sky Sports

Semi-Final 2 - Saturday 26 September, Wigan Warriors v TBC, 5.30pm KO on Sky Sports

The Super League play-offs are under way, live on Sky Sports, and continues all the way through until the Grand Final from Old Trafford on October 3.

articles.body:
On Friday night, the Atlanta Braves will begin a three-game series against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park.

Most recently, the Braves lost 8-4 on Wednesday against the Chicago Cubs .

Shortstop Ha-Seong Kim went 0-for-3 during Wednesday's loss.

Atlanta Braves Announce Ha-Seong Kim Decision

Ahead of the series opener against the Houston Astros, the Atlanta Braves have announced their starting lineup.

Underdog MLB posted on X: "Braves 9/18 D. Baldwin DH R. Acuña Jr. RF M. Olson 1B M. Harris II CF M. Dubón SS O. Albies 2B M. Yastrzemski LF A. Riley 3B S. Murphy C T. Mahle SP"

After Wednesday's hitless performance, Ha-Seong Kim has returned to the team's bench. Kim has now gone hitless in his last four appearances for the Braves.

While the shortstop improved marginally over the past month, his offensive struggles have continued as he has been unable to perform well offensively in any sustained period this season.

The Braves shortstop is batting .123 with 14 hits, one double, eight runs, nine RBIs and two stolen bases in 46 games.

Kim signed a one-year, $20 million contract with the Atlanta Braves this offseason, after previously playing 24 games for them during the 2025 season. Kim posted a .253 batting average with the Braves in those 24 games.

After dropping two out of three against the Chicago Cubs, the Atlanta Braves fell to 89-64. They still hold a four-game lead over the Philadelphia Phillies in the National League East, and hold the tiebreaker. Atlanta's magic number to clinch the division title is five games. The Braves have gone 4-6 over their last 10 games.

Right-hander Tyler Mahle is set to make his eighth start of the season for Atlanta. Mahle has been stellar since joining Atlanta, as he's posted a 3-1 record and a 1.25 ERA in 43.1 innings for the Braves this season.

Meanwhile, the Houston Astros have also announced their starting lineup for Friday's series opener.

Underdog MLB posted on X: "Astros 9/18 J. Peña SS Y. Alvarez DH I. Paredes 3B J. Altuve 2B D. Varsho CF C. Walker 1B T. Trammell RF L. Wade Jr. LF C. Vázquez C P. Lambert SP"

At 77-76, the Houston Astros hold a one-game lead over the Texas Rangers in the American League West. The Astros have gone 4-6 over their last 10 games.

articles.title: The Prediction: Eastern Washington Eagles
articles.summary: The UWDP staff make their predictions for Week 3
articles.body:
It's week 3, and the Huskies will attempt to right the ship against the Big Sky's Eastern Washington Eagles! Our staff has their predictions below!

Forty-two-point-five points??? Did the oddsmakers see what Washington did offensively over the last two weeks? Sure, the Huskies haven't played FCS competition, but they should have physical advantages over Washington St and Utah St that were never apparent when they had the ball. Winning a game by six TDs obviously requires a team to score at least six TDs and the Dawgs have done nothing through two weeks to indicate that could be attainable.

QB Nate Bell has carried the offense with 260 passing yards per game. However, Eastern has struggled in the trenches and the UW defensive line should be able to get penetration and make him uncomfortable. The Eagles have only averaged 3.7 yards per carry against three FCS teams and the UW defense has been fantastic against better opposition.

The bigger question is whether the offense can start to right the ship. They have not blocked well and they continue to lose skill position players who could make up for the lack of great blocking. Rashid Williams has joined Christian Moss, Jordan Washington, Jayden Limar, and Quaid Carr on the list of walking wounded. Demond Williams has been erratic so far and his depth options are getting thinner. I expect the outcome to be a step in the right direction. I think the offensive line has the talent to play better and there is still good talent at WR. However, I don't think there's anything near enough attacking talent to win by 42.5.

Here in week 3, it is currently the worst I've ever felt about this team after a 2-0 start. Injuries are piling up in the worst spots, the offensive line has no push up front so we can't run the ball, and Demond Williams has shown little improvement over last year. Again it's still early, but I'm running out of patience for the offense. This game, then, against the FCS Eastern Washington Eagles, will mark a turning point for the unit. Either they get it together and get some positive momentum against an easy opponent, or they sink deeper into the mire of mediocrity. I sincerely hope the positive outcome is the one we see on Saturday. For that to happen though, Demond's going to have to stay calm and not force the big play, and the line is going to have to bully the Eagles' front. If they can do that, then maybe they'll get back to how I thought they'd look coming into the year! Not sure how much that's worth against an FCS team, but hopefully that can be a springboard toward something positive.

Defensively, Eastern likes to throw, and the dual threat Nate Bell will be a tough cover. However, he's short a few of his wide receivers, and the onus for the offense will fall largely on him and his running backs, and ultimately, this defense has too much talent to give up much in the way of field position. I expect an easy win, but not a cover, as 42.5 is too much for this offense at this point.

I've predicted consecutive blowouts and Washington has not delivered. So why would I do it a third time? The Huskies are favored by a whopping 42.5. The Huskies haven't scored 42 points total this season… against two bad opponents, mind you. That said, EWU is not the EWU of old. The field still appears vibrant red on television, but the quality of play on that field has dipped. Still, EWU remains dangerous because it resides in the Evergreen State so there will be no shortage of motivation as it takes on the biggest brand in the state. For that reason, Washington can not give EWU any hope or it will be on upset alert rather quickly. I think the Huskies win this game, but I think it's another weekend that's too close for comfort. Washington hasn't "survived" yet. As in there hasn't been a game that felt like it was going to result in a loss, only for the Huskies to win it in the end. I think that happens this weekend. Washington will find more success on offense than then the previous two weeks, but not enough to win comfortably.

Straight Up : Washington – 3, Eastern Washington – 0

Against The Spread : Washington-0, Eastern Washington – 3

Average Score : Washington – 30, Eastern Washington-13.33

As always, leave your predictions in the comments below! Go Dawgs!

articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are pushing towards 100 wins for the 2026 MLB season. Standing in their way presently are the Baltimore Orioles . Meanwhile, the Brewers announced a sudden decision on Cooper Pratt before that series began.

The Brewers have already clinched the NL Central division, as they have a 10-game lead over the Chicago Cubs . However, it wouldn't hurt to put more distance between them and the rest of the division as the playoffs approach.

Milwaukee Brewers Announce Sudden Cooper Pratt Decision Before Game 1 Of New Series Versus The Baltimore Orioles

Prior to the first game of this three-game series against the AL East's Orioles, the Brewers announced multiple lineup decisions, including Pratt's.

"Brewers 9/18: J. Chourio LF B. Turang 2B W. Contreras C A. Vaughn 1B C. Yelich DH J. Ortiz 3B G. Mitchell CF L. Lara RF C. Pratt SS D. May SP," Underdog MLB announced the Brewers lineup on social media.

Friday night's lineup includes a few major changes, including the addition of 22-year-old Pratt .

Sal Frelick , David Hamilton , Gary Sanchez , and Bo Naylor are all players who are coming out. Coming back into the lineup alongside Pratt are Christian Yelich , Garrett Mitchell , and William Contreras .

Looking At Cooper Pratt Since His Benching Incident Against The New York Mets

The rookie hit a rough patch during a game against the New York Mets. However, since then, he has rebounded nicely.

In 13 games in September, he has recorded 14 hits, nine RBIs, and two stolen bases. Additionally, Pratt has been batting .311 with a .367 on-base percentage.

Following the benching incident against the Mets, Pratt took responsibility for his lapse in judgment.

"There is no excuse," Pratt said via ESPN . "I should've ran hard no matter if it's foul or fair, if it's an out. I should've been busting my butt to get to second base. Some of the guys pulled me aside and let me know, 'Hey, this is how we do it here,' and I know that. It won't happen again. There's a certain way to play here and I may be new, but it doesn't matter."

"It's the way we're right through the organization from rookie ball to the big leagues. And I didn't do that. And I will do that. No excuses."

This will surely be one of many exciting games to end off the 2026 regular season.

articles.title: Dodgers welcome back Edwin Díaz from the IL after a month out with a neck injury
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Díaz came off the injured list Friday after missing a month with a neck injury.  The 32-year-old right-hander was available...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Díaz came off the injured list Friday after missing a month with a neck injury.

The 32-year-old right-hander was available out of the bullpen for the series opener against San Francisco .

Díaz is 2-2 with an 11.85 ERA in 16 games with the Dodgers. He signed with the team as a free agent last offseason.

He made five rehab appearances during his second IL stint of the season. Díaz allowed six runs and had four strikeouts in 4 1/3 innings.

Right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, a day after throwing four scoreless innings in a victory over the Cincinnati Reds .

articles.title: 4 bold predictions for Chargers against Raiders in Week 2
articles.summary: Here are four bold predictions for the Chargers ahead of their Week 2 matchup against the Raiders.
articles.body:
The Chargers will look to avoid a 0-0-2 hole this week as they host the Raiders at SoFi Stadium.

Los Angeles has a chance to bounce back in a big way and finally get a win after an abysmal outing against the Cardinals.

Week 1 often lies, but we'll soon find out whether the Chargers ' performance last week was a fluke or a glimpse of what this team could be. For their sake, they'd better hope it was the former.

Either way, Week 2 offers Los Angeles a golden opportunity to put its first win of the season on the board and get back on track.

Here are four bold predictions for the Chargers that could ultimately lead to their first win of 2026.

Justin Herbert throws three touchdown passes

We didn't see Mike McDaniel's transcendent offense in Week 1, but I think we'll see it against the Raiders in Week 2.

Justin Herbert will be the biggest beneficiary. After throwing for only one touchdown in Week 1, I think he'll collect three, all through the air. With or without Ladd McConkey , who is listed as questionable, I think we'll see the McDaniel offense we expected from the start.

I think the defense bounces back in a big way and commits their first handful of turnovers after not collecting any in Week 1.

This team is too talented on defense to not go another week without committing a turnover. On top of that, Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins threw two interceptions against the lowly Dolphins .

A more talented Chargers team should hit that total or even surpass it.

Omarion Hampton scores two touchdowns, goes for 100+ rushing yards

Hampton started Week 1 hot but cooled off significantly after the Chargers' first drive.

The 23-year-old recorded only 43 yards on the ground, and while he scored a touchdown, it was a poor performance.

I think Hampton scores twice, and I think he also runs it down the Raiders' throats. Las Vegas held the Dolphins' De'Von Achane to 36 rushing yards, so it won't be easy for Hampton to do that, but it is doable.

Genesis Smith records his first career interception

Smith, the Week 1 standout, will get some more shine in Week 2 after Elijah Molden was ruled out. I think he will take full advantage of it.

Smith will find himself in a meaningful defensive role in a pivotal AFC West game and make Cousins and the Raiders' offense pay.

articles.title: 3 burning Blue Jackets questions entering 2026-27 NHL season
articles.summary: The Columbus Blue Jackets had a publicly dramatic endin g to the 2025-26 NHL season. The Blue Jackets were close to making the Stanley Cup Playoffs last year...
articles.body:
The Columbus Blue Jackets had a publicly dramatic ending to the 2025-26 NHL season. The Blue Jackets were close to making the Stanley Cup Playoffs last year. They missed due to some poor performances. Those poor performances did not sit well with head coach Rick Bowness .

Initially brought in as a stopgap coach, Bowness returns to the Blue Jackets for the upcoming 2026-27 campaign. He ripped into Columbus players at the end of last season. That did not stop the franchise from bringing him back this summer.

Bowness promised change at the end of last season. He will have a chance to implement that change. However, some of the changes made to this team may happen against his wishes. Especially if this summer is any indication.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Blue Jackets nearly traded Zach Werenski to the Dallas Stars this summer after difficult contract negotiations. Additionally, winger Kirill Marchenko told the team he will not play for them beyond his current contract. These are two of the team's most important players who have uncertain futures with the team.

The puck is about to drop on the new season, though. With this in mind, here are three burning questions surrounding the Columbus Blue Jackets before 2026-27.

What does change look like for Rick Bowness?

Rick Bowness talked a big game about enacting change this upcoming season. He was not pleased with how his team carried itself at the end of last season. His task now is to instill a new culture and a new attitude in Columbus.

This is a big undertaking, especially for a coach who was retired for a few years prior to joining the Blue Jackets. Bowness is a veteran, so he has seen a lot in his days in hockey. At the same time, the game is not the same as it used to be.

Can Bowness connect with these players? Can he get them to buy in on the changes he wishes to make? And what exactly does change for the veteran bench boss actually look like?

Can Zach Werenski move on from summer drama?

For a few weeks in the summer, it seemed as if Zach Werenski was going to be traded. When the news broke of his near-trade to the Dallas Stars, it wasn't entirely surprising. The surprising part was that Werenski himself stepped in to decline the trade.

The Blue Jackets defenseman had a change of heart at the last minute. He decided he did not want to leave the only NHL team he had ever known. He is focused on winning and doing so with the Blue Jackets.

Werenski's trade saga played out in public. So much so that it had to be resolved with public statements from Werenski and general manager Don Waddell. Can Werenski put this whole thing behind him? Or will this continue to linger into the 2026-27 campaign?

Will Kirill Marchenko be traded midseason?

The situation around Kirill Marchenko is certainly interesting. Reports emerged over the summer that he had no intention of signing long-term with the Blue Jackets. On Friday, this whole thing took a turn when the star winger evaded questions about whether he enjoyed playing in Columbus.

"I don't want to give you guys a lot of things. I love my teammates, I love to enjoy the practices, enjoy the hockey … it's my favorite thing in the world. I just do my job," the Blue Jackets star said, via Aaron Portzline of The Athletic.

It's hard to brush things like this aside. Marchenko is under contract for the 2026-27 campaign before reaching restricted free agency next summer. He sees the light at the end of the tunnel, and it appears he's excited to reach that light.

Will the Blue Jackets trade Marchenko during the season? Or will they make one more push to sign their star winger, even if it's just a bridge contract that takes him to unrestricted free agency in 2028?

articles.title: Bears-Vikings Franchise Connections
articles.summary: Let’s spotlight the franchise connections between the Bears and Vikings heading into Week 2. @jacobinfante24 has it here:
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears will look to continue their winning ways and improve to 2-0 on Sunday, when they take on the Minnesota Vikings in Chicago's home opener at Soldier Field. In an NFC North division where all four teams figure to compete for a playoff spot, every win you can acquire within the division is a crucial one.

Each week going forward, we're going to highlight some of the connections that the Bears' coaching staff and roster each have with the Vikings, as well as Minnesota's ties to Chicago. As one could expect between two divisional foes, there's certainly some overlap between the two organizations.

Heading into Week 2, the Bears have three players from their 53-man roster who have previously played on the Vikings. The most notable of the three is Case Keenum , who started 14 games at quarterback for the Vikings in 2017. Minnesota went 11-3 with him as their starter and advanced to the NFC Championship Game. To Vikings fans, he'll forever be remembered as the quarterback who hit Stefon Diggs for that game-winning touchdown against the Saints , dubbed as the "Minneapolis Miracle".

Safety Xavier Woods, who missed Week 1 for the Bears but is anticipated to return, also spent a season with the Vikings. He spent 2021 with Minnesota, starting in all 17 games. He finished the season with 108 tackles, three interceptions, ten pass deflections, and two forced fumbles. That year, Woods ranked No. 33 in the NFL with a 76.7 PFN SAF Impact Score , generally ranking him as an average starter at the position.

The two current Bears players to be drafted by the Vikings are center Garrett Bradbury , who was a first-round selection by Minnesota in 2019, and defensive lineman James Lynch, who was a fourth-round pick in 2020. Bradbury spent six seasons with the team as its starting center, having started in all 88 games he played there. Though the Vikings declined his fifth-year option in 2022, they signed Bradbury to a three-year, $15.7 million extension in 2023. He was released before his third and final year of the contract played out.

Lynch spent four seasons in Minnesota, appearing in 37 games and starting in three. He missed the entire 2023 season due to a torn ACL, but he served as part of the Vikings' defensive line rotation, combining for 53 tackles and 2.0 sacks in the games he played.

If we want to get technical, practice squad defensive end Marcus Davenport also has ties to the Vikings, having spent his 2023 season with them. He signed a one-year, $13 million deal but only appeared in four games due to injury.

The only player currently on the Vikings who has played for the Bears is long snapper Andrew DePaola . He played in 16 games for Chicago in 2017, when Patrick Scales tore his ACL in the preseason of that year. Once Scales returned to the team, DePaola had brief stints with the Raiders and Panthers before signing with Minnesota in 2020. There, he grew into one of the best long snappers in the NFL. He is a four-time All-Pro and a three-time Pro Bowler across his seven seasons with the Vikings.

The most notable behind-the-scenes overlap between the Bears and Vikings is Ryan Pace, who currently serves as a football advisor for Minnesota but is best known for his seven seasons as Chicago's general manager from 2015 to 2021. During that span, the Bears went 48-65 under Pace, making the playoffs twice and winning the NFC North in 2018. Though that 2018 team fielded an incredible defense, the Bears were unable to make it past the Wild Card Round. The less said about that game, the better.

Well, I suppose there's also Chicago team president Kevin Warren, who spent over a decade in the Vikings' front office, but most Bears fans are tired of hearing about him.

articles.body:
Todd Boehly is out at Chelsea , taking with him some memes and some memories which will live forever… or at least for a few years.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

It's Chelsea – Brentford this evening, but off the pitch there are even bigger things happening.

This week, just 10 days or so after whispers began, Clearlake Capital bought out the stakes of Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in Chelsea. That means the American investment group now control the whole club in terms of governance, if not equity.

Walter was never a public figure with the Blues – he had enough going on elsewhere. But Boehly was the face of the takeover, and we all knew his name long before we knew about Behdad Eghbali, Jose Feliciano or anyone else.

Boehly wanted washed up Ronaldo – Tuchel said no

The Athletic have done a fun run-down of the chaotic Boehly-era. While he faded into the background in the last two years, there were some standout moments.

There's a retelling of how close Chelsea were to signing Cristiano Ronaldo in 2022 after a meeting with Jorge Mendes:

"Multiple sources told The Athletic that Boehly came away from that encounter highly intrigued by the possibility of signing Mendes' star client Cristiano Ronaldo, who was then dissatisfied in his second spell at Manchester United , but Thomas Tuchel, Chelsea's head coach at the time, made clear on several occasions his strong opposition to any deal for the Portuguese forward."

Just another thing to thank Thomas Tuchel for…

Clearlake are now sole owners of Chelsea, and the future of the club is now entirely in their hands. Here's what they've got in mind.

Xabi Alonso's predicted team for tonight is forced into some injury changes, and faces a tough battle against Brentford.

articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 Live Updates: The Asian Games 2026 have begun in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with India entering the continental showpiece aiming to build
articles.body:
Indian double Olympic medalist and Asian Games gold medalist shooter Manu Bhaker expressed happiness at being one of the flag-bearers for the Indian contingent for the Asian Games 2026 opening ceremony, saying that it feels "heartwarming". The star shooter also recalled some special memories attached with opening ceremonies at multi-sporting events.

Manu Bhaker and kabaddi star Pawan Sehrawat will be India's flag-bearers for the Asian Games opening ceremony which will take place on Saturday.

Speaking in a video ahead of the ceremony, Bhaker said that realising that she was chosen as one of the flag-bearers left her with a "heartwarming" feeling, and all she could experience was flashbacks of her early days in the sport and reflecting on how far she has come.

"Honestly, when I found out yesterday, I had all these flashback memories of my earlier days. And, you know, when I started, I never thought that this was where I could reach one day in my sport. So, it is definitely a very heartwarming feeling. I feel really proud, really honoured, and really, really happy to be chosen as the flag bearer for my country. I just want to say thank you to God and thank you to everyone for all the love and support," she said.

Manu said that during her first Asian Games back in 2018, she was a teenager and missed the opening ceremony. She recalled attending the opening ceremony for the 2018 Commonwealth Games and being told by her coach and late shooting legend Jaspal Rana not to attend the opening ceremonies if she was not a flag-bearer, due to how the event could take a toll on her physical health ahead of her matches.

"I remember I was 16 years old during my first Asian Games, and this is my third. My first one was in Jakarta, though we were in Palembang, which was really far from the main village, so we couldn't attend. The first ceremony I ever attended was at the Commonwealth Games. After that, my coach, Jaspal Sir, told me, "If you are the flag bearer, then I will allow you to attend the ceremonies; otherwise, no," because our matches usually start on Day one or Day two, so it gets very hectic for us in shooting," she recalled.

"Usually, our competitions start right the day after the opening ceremony. So after that, it turned out that every time I attended an opening ceremony, I was either holding the flag or watching it on TV. It feels very nostalgic because I never imagined I would be here one day. Sports are just amazing! That is all I have to say right now," she added.

Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha attended the official welcome reception for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, where she met Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani and other members of the Asian sporting fraternity.

Sharing pictures from the gathering on X, Usha described the evening as an opportunity to connect with the OCA leadership and members of the wider sporting community.

“A wonderful evening connecting with the OCA President HE Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani and the esteemed members of the OCA Family at the official welcome reception. Together, we continue to pave the way for the growth and excellence of sports across Asia,” Usha wrote in an X post.

The reception was held ahead of the Asian Games opening ceremony, scheduled for Saturday at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games will bring together athletes from across the continent, with India set to compete in multiple sporting disciplines.

Olympic Council of Asia President HE Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani also led the 110th OCA Executive Board meeting in Nagoya, Japan, prior to the Asian Games.

Taiwan sport minister Lee Yang, a former Olympic badminton champion, was initially blocked from attending a flag-raising ceremony at the Games on Friday, triggering a standoff as the Taiwan delegation refused to participate in protest.

Lee was eventually permitted entry, with the ceremony taking place more than an hour after scheduled. Taiwan's cabinet complained Lee had been subject to "unreasonable obstruction" in a statement and that he had obtained the required access credentials.

Sheikh Joaan said at a press conference he was unaware of the incident but that politicians needed to stay out of sports at the quadrennial Games.

"I think that our focus here is on the athletes and on making sure that everyone, all the athletes, have the equal rights in competing and in having their freedom," the Qatari told reporters in Nagoya.

"So I don't think the politicians or politics should be involved in sports. That's my opinion."

Indian shot put athlete Tajinderpal Singh Toor will be replaced by kabaddi star Pawan Sehrawat as the male flag-bearer for the Asian Games opening ceremony on Saturday.

As per the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), due to technical issues, two-time Asian Games champion Tajinder will no longer be the flagbearer and the Asian Games 2022 gold medalist, Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) star Pawan will be taking his place.

Manu Bhaker, the Asian Games gold medalist and double Olympic medalist, will stay as the women's flag-bearer for the Indian contingent.

Manu and Tajinderpal were initially announced as the flag-bearers for the women's contingent on Saturday.

Bhaker, who won two bronze medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics, will compete in the women’s 10m air pistol, women’s 25m pistol, and 10m Air Pistol Mixed Team. She made history in Paris by becoming the first athlete from independent India to win two medals in a single edition of the Olympic Games.

Pawan, now the male flag-bearer, will be aiming to lead India to another gold medal in men's kabaddi. Since the debut of the sport in men's team competition at the 1990 Asian Games, India has won gold at eight out of nine editions, except for a bronze medal finish in the 2018 edition in Australia. In the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games edition, India beat Iran 33-29 to capture the gold medal in men's competition.

articles.title: Washington Football Players Return to Honor Late Teammate
articles.summary: During the first quarter in Saturday's 16-14 win over Utah State the Washington Huskies football team honored former defensive lineman Voi Tunuufi.
articles.body:
Several former Washington Huskies returned to Montlake over the weekend as the team honored the late Voi Tunuufi during the first half in Saturday's 16-14 win over Utah State.

Tunuufi, a defensive lineman who played 52 games for the Huskies from 2021-24, died in a car accident near his hometown of South Jordan, Utah, on May 4. Dozens of his teammates, including Devin Culp , Richard Newton, Drew Fowler, Alphonzo Tuputala, and Jackson Girouard, got together after the Huskies' afternoon victory Saturday to pay respects after Tunuufi was honored at Husky Stadium during a television timeout in the first quarter.

Former edge rushers coach Eric Schmidt, Tunuufi's position coach under then-coach Kalen DeBoer, who is now the head coach at North Dakota, offered his thoughts on X (formerly Twitter) before delivering a thrashing 47-23 win over Portland State. Tunuufi's parents had a detailed mural made in their basement that other former UW football players have shared on social media, including Lance Holtzclaw, who now plays nearby at the University of Utah.

In his four seasons at UW, the former standout defensive lineman from East High School suited up for three different coaches and was one of a handful of players to return to the school to play for Jedd Fisch after the run to the national championship game in DeBoer's final season.

From a tumultuous 2021 season with Jimmy Lake at the helm as a freshman, which saw Tunuufi appear in 11 games with two starts. His first start came at Arizona against Fisch's Wildcats, a comeback 21-16 win in Tucson, and his second came against Oregon later in the year.

Tunuufi's early success blossomed in the following two seasons. He proved to be a key rotational defensive lineman, making several crucial plays, including sacks against then-No. 11 Michigan State, Arizona, and in the 2022 Alamo Bowl against Texas.

In total, the ever-present defender finished his career with 86 tackles, 15.5 tackles for loss, 12.5 sacks, and a forced fumble. As impressive and impactful as his numbers were, however, his name and No. 52 will certainly never be forgotten on the shores of Montlake and wherever his former teammates, coaches, and family are.

articles.title: Heavy Doses Of Ashton Jeanty Could Be Formula For Raiders' Success In Las Vegas This Season
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have seemingly found a winning formula by heavily utilizing running back Ashton Jeanty.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders may havefound a recipe for success in their Week 1 home win over the Miami Dolphins ,27-13. In first-yearhead coach Klint Kubiak's first game on the Raiders sideline, the teamleaned heavily on second-year running back Ashton Jeanty . This heavy dose of Jeantyproved to be a difference-maker in the Raiders getting off to a 1-0 start in2026.

Jeanty shoulderedmuch of the load in Week 1 for this new, seemingly improved Raiders offense. The2025 No. 6 overall pick carried the ball 23 times for 102 yards in the win overMiami and added six receptions for 45 yards and two touchdowns. He led the teamin rushing yards, receptions, and receiving yards on 29 total touches.

Kubiakpresented an extremely balanced attack offensively, as quarterback Kirk Cousins recorded30 passes in the game. Jeanty's 147 scrimmage yards went a long way in helpingthe Raiders control the tempo and flow of the game.

Of course,it was the Dolphins they beat up on in Week 1. So, despite having a last-placeschedule based on their finish last season, the Raiders have some toughmatchups moving forward through the first half of the 2026 campaign.

Las Vegas goes on the road in Weeks 2 & 3 to face the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints . Those feellike winnable games, but you never know how things will go in divisional games,and Tyler Shough seems to be showing more promise with every game he plays forNew Orleans. Weeks 4 through 11 could decide the fate of Kubiak's first seasonas coach in Vegas.

Starting withWeek 4, the Raiders face the Kansas City Chiefs , New England Patriots , Buffalo Bills , Los Angeles Rams , New York Jets , San Francisco 49ers , Seattle Seahawks , and Denver Broncos before a post-Thanksgiving Week 12 showdown in Cleveland with the Browns before the bye in Week 13. The Raiders did beat New Englandto open last season, but that was before the Pats got rolling under then-newhead coach Mike Vrabel, winning 13 of their final 14 games en route to a SuperBowl appearance.

While thislooks like a tough stretch on paper, establishing a balanced attack againstthese teams will be key. Cousins is known for slinging the ball all over thefield, but it's time for Jeanty to put the offense on his back. Out of the gatethis season, Jeanty hit the 100-yard mark after doing it just twice in hisrookie season.

It took Jeanty fourgames last season before he even sniffed a 100-yard performance. That Week 4game against the Chicago Bears last season remains Jeanty's career-high at 138yards. If the Raiders are going to have success this year and surprise teams,it'll balance between run and pass on offense, but ultimately a Jeanty-heavy game plan each week should be the mode to make the Raiders even a semi-threatin the AFC.

articles.title: What Will Yankees Do With Lineup If Judge Can Only DH In Postseason?
articles.summary: Aaron Judge is headed to the injured list with a calf strain
articles.body:
The New York Yankees will reportedly place Aaron Judge on the injured list on Saturday with a calf strain, seriously putting his postseason availability in doubt.

Judge will be ineligible to return until the final game of the regular season. If his injury is minor and the Yankees are just being cautious, he should be good to go for the postseason. However, what will the Yankees do if Judge is ready for the postseason but not quite ready to play in the field?

It's very possible that if Judge is healthy enough to swing a bat that the Yankees will slot him in as the designated hitter. Even if his timing is not quite back, he's still Aaron Judge, and the Yankees are not going to keep him out of a postseason lineup if he can play. If Judge is in the lineup as the designated hitter, it creates a huge lineup shuffle for Aaron Boone.

Cody Bellinger , Heliot Ramos and Spencer Jones will likely man the outfield, but Judge serving as the designated hitter could have a bigger impact on the infield. Ben Rice has been serving as the Yankees' designated hitter, with Luis Garcia Jr. at first base.

Garcia has started all but seven games since the Yankees got him, and he has been great. He has a .285 batting average with seven home runs as a Yankee. 32 of his appearances have come at first base, but if Judge is serving as the designated hitter, Rice would go to first base. Garcia is too good a hitter to be out of the lineup, so the Yankees may have to move him to second base. Garcia played 129 games at second base last year, and has 508 career appearances there.

If Garcia is at second base, the Yankees then have to make a decision with Jazz Chisholm Jr. , Anthony Volpe and Ryan McMahon . McMahon is not a good hitter, but plays great defense at third base. Volpe has been a terrible hitter for most of his career, but he is hitting .348 since being recalled after his demotion in August. The Yankees had Volpe play some third base during his demotion.

Chisholm has experience at third base in the big leagues and started games there for the Yankees in the 2024 run to the World Series. He has not had the best year offensively, but has turned things around in the last month. Since Aug. 4, Chisholm has a .832 OPS. The only problem is that he is also on the injured list, and if he does not get some in-game at-bats before the postseason, there will be no way to know if he is ready to go for the postseason.

Ultimately, the Yankees simply have to wait and see where Judge and Chisholm are with their injuries when the postseason rolls around.

articles.title: Brewers recall left-hander Colton Gordon for additional bullpen depth
articles.summary: The Brewers recalled left-hander Colton Gordon from Class AAA Nashville on Sept. 18 and optioned right-hander Garrett Stallings out.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE – The Milwaukee Brewers will get their first up-close look at the Colton Gordon , the second and more intriguing piece of their July 15 trade with the Houston Astros that also brought them Lance McCullers Jr. after recalling him from Class AAA Nashville on Friday, Sept. 18.

The left-hander joins the bullpen for the immediate future with right-hander Garrett Stallings being optioned to Nashville in the corresponding move.

"Super excited," Gordon said prior to the Brewers' series opener against the Baltimore Orioles . "Obviously, the Brewers are a winning organization and I love to win. That's what I've done my whole life, and to be able to help an organization do that, get as far as we can go, whatever role that is for me I'm just excited to be a part of that.

"I appreciated my time in Houston. A lot of good friends, and coaches and staff who have helped me along the way, but always excited for new opportunities."

Gordon, 27, was 1-5 with a 4.67 ERA and WHIP of 1.28 in 10 starts for the Sounds and 48 strikeouts in 54 innings.

He started 14 games a season ago and one this season with four total appearances for the Astros before being traded over to the Brewers in exchange for minor-leaguer Jadyn Fielder.

"A guy the organization went after, and so you do your research and watch the video and all that kind of stuff," manager Pat Murphy said. "He's a consummate pitcher. You look for the sweeper to be a big pitch for him, and for him to locate his heater."

The Brewers were in need of a fresh arm after Stallings threw three innings in the Brewers' 7-4 loss to the Pirates on Sept. 17, a strong performance that saw him record a career-high six strikeouts.

"He's fantastic," Murphy said of Stallings. "It's Bryse Wilson , it's Brent Suter , it's all those guys that are just key to their ballclub. The kid has been amazing, he really has."

There will be other moving parts in the bullpen in the coming days as well with Wilson and Grant Anderson both nearing returns from the injured list.

Gordon, meanwhile, jumps aboard a Brewers team that continues to rocket toward a first-round postseason bye with eyes on finishing with the best record in baseball for the second straight year.

"It's awesome," he said. "It's exciting to be a part of that, and I want to help in any way I can. I'm happy to be here and I want to keep it going."

"Just staying ready, competing, trying to win ballgames," Gordon said.

articles.title: Maryland women’s soccer falls to Penn State, 2-0, for third straight defeat
articles.summary: The Terps have been held scoreless in five of their last six games.
articles.body:
Maryland women's soccer returned home from a winless West Coast trip for its Big Ten home opener against Penn State, but the Hollywood script largely stayed the same for the Terps.

After falling behind from an early goal, Maryland's offense struggled throughout, en route to a third straight shutout in a 2-0 defeat to the Nittany Lions.

Penn State's offense barraged the Terps' goal with chances right out of the gate. Within the first seven minutes, the Nittany Lions had attempted six shots — five coming on goal.

It looked like Penn State would capitalize on its offensive onslaught. Paige Pasinski beat Faith Luckey with a dribble move for what appeared to be an open shot on goal, but Paige Foye stepped in front to block Pasinski's shot.

Seconds later, Luckey made an outstanding defensive play of her own, diving to get her fingertips on the ball and deflect it out of bounds.

Maryland came back down with some offense of its own, something the Terps had been lacking in Big Ten play. McKinley Heaven and Dani Gichner each found space and fired shots that required Penn State goalkeeper Mackenzie Gress to make difficult saves.

After opening the game with a wave of offense, Penn State managed to break through the Terps' defense in the 19th minute. Luckey had recorded saves on the first five shots on goal, but Paige Kalal found the back of the net with the sixth.

"I think we started the game poorly." head coach Michael Marchiano said. "I think we lacked the organization and the coordination necessary to defend against a team like Penn State."

Despite the early offensive barrage, the Terps' defense found their footing during the remainder of the first half.

It looked like Maryland's defensive rhythm would remain coming out of the break, but after being held shotless to start the second half, Penn State took advantage of its first chance coming out of the break.

The Nittany Lions refound their crisp passing that aided the offensive attack in the first half, and after being denied on her first four shots, Pasinski found the back of the net to double Penn State's lead in the 62nd minute.

That lead nearly grew just minutes later, with Penn State awarded a penalty kick on a foul from Gichner in the box.

Aubrey Kulpa stepped up to take the shot, but Luckey was up to the task and saved the first penalty kick from an opponent this season.

Despite allowing multiple goals, Luckey put up a strong performance, something that has been a trend during Big Ten play. She made eight saves, including the penalty stop. However, again, Luckey was given no room for error from the Terps' attack.

"I think we need our goalkeeper to make big saves, and obviously the penalty kick… she comes up with a big save," Marchiano said. "As we're building this program and trying to increase our level, we need a goalkeeper who can make saves, keep us in games, and help us win games as we go forward."

Jolie Farmer, Maryland's top goalscorer, made her first appearance since Sep. 3 against Old Dominion. Farmer had missed time with injury, and in that stretch, the Terps' offense struggled mightily.

While Farmer did not make an impact in the first half, the Terps turned to her early and often in the second half.

As Maryland looked to create opportunities on offense, Farmer was at the heart of the efforts. She was the recipient of multiple passes on runs toward the Penn State box and stretched the defense to create open space but couldn't log a shot.

In the 57th minute, Farmer generated a chance for Lisa McIntyre, whose run resulted in the Terps' first chance of the second half, but McIntyre's shot went well wide.

Farmer subbed back into the game late into the second half, and after an extended period without any attacking pressure, the Terps' offense looked much better with her on the field.

Farmer had an opportunity of her own in the 86th minute, as she battled through contact to deliver a shot towards the Penn State goal that Gress saved.

Despite the addition of Farmer to the field, Maryland's offense struggled following its early opportunities. After opening the game with two early shots on goal, the Terps mustered just two more for the remainder of the game.

"Again, we need to be really efficient when we play these games." Marchiano said. "Nobody's given up here by any means. We're going to keep trying to improve, and that's the message to the girls."

1. Good signs from Jolie Farmer. While the Terps' offense struggled overall for a third straight game, Farmer looked good in her first game back from injury. Maryland is going to need her to regain her goalscoring form, but if she does, it could be the key breakthrough for the Terps' offense.

2. Multiple players return from injury. Farmer was not the only Terp that returned to make an impact after dealing with an injury. Taryn Raibon played just 16 minutes against Oregon after missing time but logged 41 minutes of play against the Nittany Lions. Raibon was a consistent starter before her injury and is a key piece for Maryland's defense.

3. Starting slow continues to cost the Terps. A recurring problem for Maryland this season has been slow starts that lead to deficits. That issue plagued the Terps again, and it cost them. Both sides of the ball will need to open the game better for Maryland to keep itself in games long enough to take advantage of any opportunities the Terps can get.

articles.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson's Week 2 game status revealed
articles.summary: The Patriots received some good news on running back TreVeyon Henderson from Friday's injury report.
articles.body:
New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson no longer has an injury designation for Sunday's Week 2 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers .

The speedy running back practiced fully on Monday for the first time since going down with an ankle injury. His return is huge news for the same Patriots offense that struggled against the Seattle Seahawks last week.

In Week 1, the Patriots were forced to lean on the combination of Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner as the top ball-carriers. Henderson possesses the kind of game-breaking speed that can ruin the best defensive game plans. articles.title: Texas linebacker coach suspended for UTSA game after arrest on DWI charges
articles.summary: Johnny Nansen will miss Saturday's game against UTSA after being charged with misdemeanor DWI on Wednesday.
articles.body:
AUSTIN - Texas linebacker coach Johnny Nansen will serve a one-game suspension and not be available to coach at the Longhorns' football home game against UTSA on Saturday night, a source told the Houston Chronicle Friday.

Nansen, 52, was charged with misdemeanor driving while intoxicated, Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said Thursday. Nansen was involved in a three-car crash in west Austin and subsequently showed signs of impairment, according to multiple reports. He is charged with a Class B misdemeanor.

"We had an unfortunate situation last evening. Coach Nansen was charged with a misdemeanor DWI," Sarkisian said Thursday. "We obviously are aware of the situation. I'm still gathering facts. I'm still monitoring the situation. We're obviously disappointed, but that's all I really have on that at this time."

Nansen has been with Texas since 2024, serving under former defensive coordinator Pete Kwiatkowski.

The Austin American-Statesman reported that Austin police responded to a three-vehicle crash on the South Capital of Texas highway at 8:55 p.m. Wednesday night. Nansen was the driver of one of the vehicles, and he "displayed signs consistent with possible impairment. Officers conducted standardized field sobriety tests and observed multiple clues of impairment."

Nansen, who serves as co-defensive coordinator with Will Muschamp, was not at the Texas practice Thursday morning.

articles.title: 'Haar nahi maanunga': Sujeet Kalkal's Asian Games 2026 gold mission on the road to LA Olympics
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: The last time Sujeet Kalkal came close to an Olympic dream, he never even got the chance to step on the mat.Now, as he prepares for his mai.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The last time Sujeet Kalkal came close to an Olympic dream, he never even got the chance to step on the mat.Now, as he prepares for his maiden Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the 23-year-old wrestler is looking at the continental event as the first major marker of a new Olympic journey - one that he hopes will eventually take him to Los Angeles in 2028.“Asaan nahi tha, bhaisaab. Fir se start kiya hai, haar nahi maanunga. Olympics to sapna hai, poora karna hai bass [It wasn’t easy. I’ve started again, and I won’t give up. The Olympics is a dream, and I have to fulfil it, that’s all],” Sujeet told TimesofIndia.com ahead of the Asian Games.There is reason for that confidence. Sujeet enters Aichi-Nagoya having established himself among the leading wrestlers in the 65kg category. He won the Asian Championships in Bishkek earlier this year and has continued to build his credentials in 2026. He also won the 65kg selection trials for the Senior World Championships in Lucknow last week, beating Anuj Kumar 8-3 in the final.The Asian Games, however, will present a different test. Sujeet's 65kg category features some of the biggest names in Asian wrestling, including Japan's Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka.Sujeet's competition starts from October 2, when the men's freestyle 65kg, 86kg and 125kg categories will be contested.For Sujeet, the Asian Games is more than just another tournament. It is a fresh start for the wrestler from Imlota village in Haryana’s Bhiwani district.“I was very happy to qualify [for the Asian Games] . It is a fresh start, and I will not disappoint. Behind this success is the hard work of my father, my coach and my entire team. I am in good form. I will come back with the gold medal,” Sujeet said.“The 65kg category is a very challenging and competitive weight category. The world’s best wrestlers always compete in this category. But I have complete faith in my hard work and preparation. My entire focus is only on gold, brother. I have worked very hard,” he added.It will also be a chance to measure how far he has travelled since April 2024, when a three-day ordeal at Dubai International Airport ended his first Olympic campaign before it had even begun.Three days at Dubai AirportIt was April 2024. Sujeet was at Dubai International Airport, waiting to continue his journey to Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, where he was scheduled to compete in the Asian Olympic Qualifying Tournament.But record rainfall had caused floods in Dubai and badly disrupted air travel.Sujeet was stranded at the airport. He could see water everywhere and could only pray that the situation would improve so he could travel to Bishkek, where the qualifiers were scheduled to take place.Sujeet could only watch the time, calculate the days and hours on his fingers, and then sit back. His connecting flight was delayed and eventually remained stranded at the airport for three days.A flight was finally arranged, but by the time he reached Kyrgyzstan and then the venue, it was one and a half hours after the weigh-in had been completed.The Wrestling Federation of India and officials tried their best to find a way to get Sujeet into the competition. But the United World Wrestling rules left them with no option.The opportunity was gone.“I felt very bad. I have no words. It was four years of hard work, and it all ended in that one moment. I was in good form, and everything was over in a moment. I cried alone too, but I had faith in God. I explained things to myself and returned to India,” Sujeet said.Father's words gave him strengthSujeet returned to India devastated. At home, his father Dayanand was waiting for him. Dayanand, a former Greco-Roman wrestler, knew what his son was going through.Sujeet immediately hugged his father. He became emotional and had his father's shoulder to cry on.His father hugged him and told him: “Koi nahi beta, fir se mehnat karenge hum, Olympics khelna hai”.Those words stayed with Sujeet.‘I didn't give up'Starting again was not easy, but Sujeet was adamant. He won gold at the United World Wrestling Ranking Series in Budapest in the men’s 65kg division at the start of 2025. He added two more gold medals to his tally in Zagreb and at the Tirana Grand Prix.He then won a gold medal at the World U23 Championships in 2025 in Novi Sad, Serbia, followed by another gold at the Asian U23 Championships in Vung Tau, Vietnam.He didn't stop there.Sujeet became Asian Champion after winning gold in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. With that gold medal finish, he also rose to the No. 1 ranking in the world.Now, he is set for his first Asian Games. A medal in Aichi-Nagoya would take him another step closer to his next big target - the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.“I didn't give up. I have worked very hard. I have to go a long way. If I had competed in Paris, I would have been 21. I am 23 now. I will be 25 when the Los Angeles Olympics comes around. Age makes a big difference. But I don't want to step back. My mindset is still the same — to win a medal for the country,” he said.'Haanikarak baapu'For Sujeet, wrestling was never just a sport. His father Dayanand, a former national wrestling champion who also represented India at the World Championships, introduced him to the sport at a very young age. Sujeet was just five when he was pushed into the 'akhaada'.Dayanand could not go to the Olympics to represent India. Now, he wants his son to fulfil that unfulfilled dream.“Papa is very strict," he says."Wo dangal mein haanikarak baapu they na, wo waise hi kuch hain (laughs). He told me, ‘Son, you have to become a wrestler. A wrestler’s son should be a wrestler.’ I have learnt a lot from him since childhood. He is both my guru and my father. Whatever I am today is because of him,” he said.“His dream is to see me at the Olympics and see me win a medal. I will definitely fulfil this dream of my father,” Sujeet signed off.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA: From Tokyo and Osaka to nearby towns such as Yokkaichi, the Indian diaspora drove down to Korogi Athletic Park on the outskirts of the city to.
articles.body: NAGOYA: From Tokyo and Osaka to nearby towns such as Yokkaichi, the Indian diaspora drove down to Korogi Athletic Park on the outskirts of the city to watch the ‘pride of India’ in action.The Indian women’s cricket team did not disappoint, making short work of the Japanese challenge for an eight-wicket victory and a place in Sunday’s semifinal against Bangladesh. The result was never really in doubt, but what was striking was the spirit of the hosts and the spunk of the travelling Indian fans.Harmanpreet Kaur-led defending champions, seemingly in no mood for batting practice, opted to bowl first and dismissed Japan for a paltry 57. But not before openers Haruna Iwasaki and Ayaka Kato-Stafford helped themselves to three boundaries between them, drawing loud applause from the home fans and the dugout.The celebratory mood continued when Nonoha Yasumoto and Ayaka Kato-Stafford claimed the wickets of G Kamalini and Bharati Fulmali. For the Indian fans, Shafali Verma provided the entertainment, smashing an unbeaten 40 off just 15 balls, including six boundaries and two sixes.The makeshift stands may have had plenty of empty seats, but the decibel levels generated by the Indian supporters more than made up for it. After all, it is not every day they get to watch their cricketing stars in action on Japanese soil.Japan-born Ishan Kumar Lal, whose parents are from New Delhi, felt the occasion could not have offered a better advertisement for cricket in the country.“Cricket in the Asian Games and India being a part of it is insanely big,” said the towering Japan U-19 all-rounder.Ishan believes matches such as these can provide a much-needed push to the sport’s growing community in Japan.“Watching big teams like these is a great motivation for us to keep doing better and keep advertising cricket in Japan and showing cricket to Japanese people living in Japan and actually make this sport a bigger sport here,” he said.With mini Japan flags fluttering in the stands, it was hard to miss the huge Indian tricolour and placards displaying the fans’ love for their team.Param Vijay Kumar, a Mysuru-born techie living in Osaka, had travelled with a group of friends.“We are grateful that a match has brought a piece of home to us. There was no way we would have missed being here,” he said.For Sukruthi Ajay, originally from Bengaluru, the occasion stirred a strong sense of patriotism.“We are here to support both countries because we love India and we respect Japan. It is a mixed match, but our heart beats for India. To watch our team play in Japan is very special. We are also huge fans of Royal Challengers Bengaluru and it was a delight to watch Smriti Mandhana and Shreyanka Patil as well,” said the homemaker-turned-content creator.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: International Sports News: Sophie Cunningham isn't one to stay quiet, and this week she finally weighed in on the Sydney Sweeney gambling ad controversy that's had social media .
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham isn't one to stay quiet, and this week she finally weighed in on the Sydney Sweeney gambling ad controversy that's had social media buzzing for days. The Indiana Fever guard tackled the topic on her podcast, calling out the campaign while still leaving room to defend Sweeney's right to cash in on her fame.Cunningham admitted she wasn't a fan of how the ad played out, questioning its authenticity from the jump. But she wasn't interested in piling on the actress either. Here's what she actually said, and why the ad drew so much heat in the first place.Sophie Cunningham joins Sydney Sweeney ad debate with her takeSophie Cunningham addressed the ongoing chatter this week, tackling it head-on during an episode of her podcast, No Hesitation With Sophie Cunningham & Drew Hanlen. She said her phone had been flooded with texts and comments from people begging her to share an opinion, so she decided it was finally time.Her first question cut straight to the point: does Sweeney even gamble on sports? "Like it's just so unauthentic," she said, laying out her skepticism about the whole campaign. Cunningham wasn't shocked by how Sweeney chose to represent the brand, noting it's simply the kind of marketing the actress has built her career on."I have so many takes, but first of all, does she even gamble on sports? Like, it's just so inauthentic. Now, here's my hot take… Why are girls mad? Like, that is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? Like… of course that's going to draw attention,” the Fever guard shared.Still, she made clear she wasn't thrilled with this particular execution, admitting she wondered what exactly the ad was trying to accomplish. Again, do I agree with it? “Morally, I think it's kind of weird, but like, to each their own. Go do your thing, sis," Cunningham added.She also pushed back on the backlash itself, wondering aloud why so many women were upset over something that's essentially just Sweeney doing what she's always done. Cunningham called the outrage a little confusing, though she said she understood why some found the ad morally odd. Despite her criticism, she was quick to add that she genuinely likes Sweeney and doesn't think women should tear each other down over choices like this. Her closing message was simple: let Sweeney make her money and do her thing.Why was Sydney Sweeney's ad controversial?The commercial in question features Sweeney posing in minimal clothing alongside sports equipment to promote a sports prediction platform, a visual pairing that got people talking almost instantly. Several athletes felt the ad leaned entirely on Sweeney's image rather than any genuine connection to sports or gambling, and that rubbed plenty of fans the wrong way.Sweeney responded to some of the criticism by sharing photos of male and female athletes who had posed n*de for ESPN The Magazine, seemingly drawing a comparison to her own shoot.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. However, Sumaya fought back, took control of the set and closed out the match 12-7 to book her place in the final.The defeat ended Quimcy’s hopes of reaching the gold-medal match, but she will have another opportunity to finish her debut Asian Games campaign on the podium.Indian had topped group with wins over Japan and CambodiaQuimcy had secured her semi-final berth after topping Group A with two wins, earning direct passage to the last four and avoiding the quarter-finals. articles.title: Chess Olympiad Round 3: Koneru Humpy downs 'Greek Goddess' Tsolakidou; Gukesh back above 2700
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: On Friday, the Indian women's team, defending champions and unbeaten so far in the tournament, was paired against Greece in Round 3 of the .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: On Friday, the Indian women's team, defending champions and unbeaten so far in the tournament, was paired against Greece in Round 3 of the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. On paper, this looked routine. India, the top seeds, were expected to win the tie, and they eventually did. But the top-board clash between Koneru Humpy and Greece's Stavroula Tsolakidou carried a subplot that had been building for a fortnight, and it turned an otherwise straightforward fixture into the day's most closely watched game.Tsolakidou was part of Ganges Grandmasters, the eventual champions of the just-concluded Global Chess League (GCL) Season 4. It was against Humpy, playing for APL Pipers, that Tsolakidou suffered her first loss of that tournament, playing white.To turn the tables in the reverse fixture, she needed something special, and got it when coach Adhiban Baskaran handed her a folder titled "Prep for the Greek Goddess!" Working off that file, she beat Humpy with the black pieces. The moniker "Greek Goddess" became famous.The two met again in the GCL final, where Tsolakidou held Humpy to a draw in the first game and then beat her again with black in the second.A positive score over the Indian, coupled with the results on the other boards, was enough to hand Ganges Grandmasters the title, with Tsolakidou also named the Player of the Tournament.So when the pairing brought them together again on Friday, it was more than a Grandmaster-versus-International Master matchup. This time, as the format shifted from rapid to classical, the Indian veteran Grandmaster prevailed.39-year-old Humpy, with white, built her position with patience. The game began as a Nimzo-Indian structure, with Humpy choosing an ambitious setup featuring 10.b4 and 11.b5, gaining queenside space.Black’s pieces became somewhat passive, while White gradually built pressure with 14.f4, 15.Qf3 and 16.Rad1.The critical phase arrived with 21.e5, opening lines and increasing the activity of White’s pieces.After 22.bxc6 bxc6, Humpy’s knight penetrated with 23.Ne4 and 24.Nxd6, winning material and creating tactical threats.The sequence 25.Nxe8 Rxe8 26.Qxh4 left White with a significant advantage, although Black’s active queen and passed-pawn kept the doors slightly open for a comeback.Humpy maintained the initiative, coordinating her rooks and bishop. 40.e6 was particularly strong, leading to 41.Bxe6+ and 42.Rd7+.After winning the f5-bishop with 43.Bxf5, White’s material and attacking advantage became decisive. Tsolakidou resigned after 46.Rf1, capping off a perfect day for the Indian Grandmaster, who had taken a rest against Finland in Round 2.Gukesh back to winning waysIn the open section, world champion D Gukesh made his way back to winning ways after Thursday's rating dip below 2700, a drop that had made headlines less for its size than for whom it happened to.Playing black against Italy's Sabino Brunello on Friday, Gukesh met a Queen's Indian-style setup.After 4...Ba6 and 5...c5, Black immediately challenged White’s queenside structure and achieved active piece play. The game became highly tactical once Gukesh expanded with 15...g5 and centralized strongly with 17...Ne4 and 19...Nd4.Brunello tried to simplify with 21.Nxd4 and 22.Rxc8, but Black’s pieces remained more active. The key sequence began with 23...Nc3, forcing exchanges that improved Black’s bishop activity. After 25...Re5, Gukesh increased the pressure, and 26...Bxe2 won an important pawn while keeping White’s king exposed.28...Bxh3 removed a key defender, while 29...Bd4+ and 30...Re2+ drove the king into a dangerous position. 31...Qxh3 left Black with overwhelming attacking threats and a large material advantage.Although Brunello gave checks with 32.Qxg5+ and 33.Qd8+, they were only temporary. Gukesh's queen and bishop combined to set up mating threats, and Brunello resigned after 33 moves, handing Gukesh a much-needed win and, with it, a step back towards the 2700 mark he had slipped under just a day earlier.India's winning streaks stay intactThe rest of India's open team also had a strong day against Italy. Praggnanandhaa and Erigaisi both drew their games, but Nihal Sarin added another win to his growing tally, beating Francesco Sonis, as India closed out the match 3-1.For India's women, Friday's 3.5-0.5 win over Greece, with only Divya Deshmukh drawing her game against Anastasia Avramidou, kept an already imposing unbeaten run alive, with Humpy, Vantika Agrawal, and Savitha Shri all winning their individual games. Vaishali Rameshbabu took a rest day.ALSO READ: The silver medal Koneru Humpy's 9-year-old daughter will remember as goldBoth Indian teams will be back in action on Saturday, with the open side facing Spain and the women's team taking on Mongolia.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Paralympic star Lauren Steadman seals Celebrity MasterChef crown after nail-biting finale
articles.summary: International Sports News: Lauren Steadman has won Celebrity MasterChef, and the Paralympic champion needed every single course to do it. Three finalists cooked a three-course m.
articles.body: Lauren Steadman has won Celebrity MasterChef, and the Paralympic champion needed every single course to do it. Three finalists cooked a three-course meal for judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli on Friday night, and only one could lift the 2026 trophy.The BBC One final capped a contest that began with 15 celebrities. Olympic medallist Emily Campbell and Love Island's Shakira Khan pushed hard, and Dent found the choice close to impossible. One dessert tipped the verdict, though, and a runner-up had a joke ready afterwards.Lauren Steadman beats Celebrity MasterChef rivals in dramatic final showdownLauren Steadman took the title on Friday, September 18, in a final shown on BBC One and iPlayer at 8 p.m. The Paralympic gold medallist beat Campbell and Khan in a head-to-head where each finalist had to cook and present a faultless three-course meal. It was the last chance to show passion and creativity in front of Dent and Locatelli, and Steadman's execution earned her the trophy.Steadman opened with scallops pan-fried in chilli butter, served with a coconut and spinach lentil dahl puree and topped with fresh apple batons. The main was a beef wellington with truffle mash, caramelised shallot, butternut squash puree, tenderstem broccoli and a red wine jus. Dessert was a classic sticky toffee pudding with dates, caramel sauce and clotted cream ice cream.The pudding did the most damage. Locatelli said, "Mamma mia... this is the best sticky toffee pudding I've ever had." Dent went with "exemplary" for the same dish and said the final plates were simply wonderful. Locatelli also explained the bigger picture. Steadman has a knack for turning every situation into an advantage, and that is why the crown went to the champion.Finals week added plenty of pressure. Steadman made a dog bone shaped dessert for fifty guests at Crufts, billed as the world's largest and most prestigious dog show. The Chef's Table at The Ritz, a top event on the culinary calendar, was another test.After the win, Steadman said, "This is up there with a Paralympic gold medal." Speechless moments are rare, Steadman added, and this was one of them.Lauren Steadman's Celebrity MasterChef win adds to a long sporting résuméSteadman is an MBE, was born in Peterborough and is a University of Portsmouth graduate. Swimming came first, at the 2008 Beijing Paralympics at age 15 and again at London 2012. Paratriathlon followed, bringing silver in Rio 2016, gold in Tokyo and bronze in Paris 2024. The three-time world champion is also an eight-time European champion.Steadman reached the Strictly Come Dancing semi-finals in 2018 as the show's first female contestant with a disability, then finished as a finalist on Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins in 2019.The kitchen was a different kind of risk, and Steadman knew it. Before the series, the athlete told the BBC that sport had taught pressure handling and a love of new challenges. Cooking for loved ones is one thing, Steadman said, and having food critically analysed is another. The show could go very wrong, but it might also build confidence. Steadman calls the style intuitive. A soup that got far too many stock cubes once became a pasta sauce, and measuring is rarely part of the routine.The other finalists took defeat well. Campbell called the result "more than deserved" and joked about being relieved that the contest was over. Khan, a runner-up on Love Island last year, said, "Always the bridesmaid, never the bride." She added that she had a ball and called Steadman's cooking a gold medal performance.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Neeraj Chopra has opened up about his latest injury setback and the disappointment of missing the Asian Games 2026 in Nagoya, admitting that being una.
articles.body: Neeraj Chopra has opened up about his latest injury setback and the disappointment of missing the Asian Games 2026 in Nagoya, admitting that being unable to represent India at an event that has produced some of the most memorable moments of his career has been difficult.The Tokyo Olympics gold medallist was among India's biggest medal hopes in the men's javelin throw, but an ankle ligament injury suffered during training forced him to pull out of both the Asian Games and the Diamond League final.Chopra's withdrawal came almost a month before the Asian Games. His most recent appearance in a major competition was at the Lausanne Diamond League Meet, where he finished second behind Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage.The 28-year-old had been chasing a third consecutive Asian Games gold after triumphs in Jakarta in 2018 and Hangzhou in 2023.“The Asian Games have given me some of the most special moments of my career, and not being able to represent India at this edition is difficult,” wrote Neeraj on the social media platform LinkedIn.“I will miss competing at the Asian Games this time. To the Indian contingent in Nagoya, I will miss walking alongside you. But I will be backing you. I have precious memories of the Games. I hope you make some too," he added.Neeraj's latest injury setbackThe ankle problem is the latest in a series of injuries that have interrupted Chopra's career over the past few years.He underwent surgery on his right elbow in 2019, while a groin injury forced him to miss the 2022 Commonwealth Games. A muscle strain affected his 2023 season before he withdrew from an event a year later because of adductor discomfort.His latest setback has now kept him out of the Asian Games.“I have been dealing with an ankle ligament injury, and after a lot of consideration, I had to accept that I will not be able to compete. Being able to carry the hope of a country into competition is a privilege. To miss out on that opportunity does hurt,” wrote Neeraj.The javelin star also reflected on the importance of having the right people around him while dealing with injuries and spending long periods away from home for training and competitions.“Injuries are a part of sport. You cannot control everything that happens to you. You can only control how you respond to it. A big part of that response is the people around me. I spend a lot of time away from home - training, travelling and competing, and over the years I’ve understood that it is important to have people around you who keep you positive and grounded. In your lowest times, you don’t really need someone to give you advice or even ask how your injury happened or how long you will be out," he added.For Chopra, that support has often come through friends who offer an escape from the constant focus on his sporting career and injuries.“Sometimes, you just need a friend to call and talk about something completely unrelated. I have friends who know I’m not in the best place right now, but when they call, they don’t ask me about my ankle. They just talk, we laugh, we remember old times, make promises to catch up; this reminds me that there is more to life than the next competition.
