articles.title: At 13, Quimcy Dsouza was a middle-distance runner before football took over; 11 years later, Ronaldinho-inspired Teqball has put her one win away from Asian Games history
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India’s Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza suffered a 1-2 defeat to Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in the women’s singles Teqball semifinal at the Asian Games 2026 on Satu.
articles.body: India’s Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza suffered a 1-2 defeat to Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in the women’s singles Teqball semifinal at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday. However, her medal hopes remain alive, with the 24-year-old set to compete for bronze against Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto on Sunday.A victory would make Quimcy the first Indian to win a Teqball medal at the Asian Games, where the sport is making its debut at the Aichi-Nagoya edition. The Indian’s journey to the last four has already been a breakthrough, marking an important chapter in her rise as one of the country’s leading Teqball players.From middle-distance running to football and TeqballHailing from Mumbai, Quimcy began her sporting journey as a middle-distance runner at the age of 13 as reported by The Indian Express. Her passion for football soon took over, and she went on to represent Maharashtra in age-group football.Although her football career did not progress as she had hoped, her love for the game remained. After completing a degree in Sports Management, she joined sports goods retailer Decathlon and discovered Teqball after watching Brazilian football legend Ronaldinho play the sport in Instagram videos.Quimcy took up the sport and gradually established herself as a leading figure in India’s Teqball community.Seven-time national champion and international trailblazerQuimcy became the first Indian woman Teqer to represent the country at the international level. She also founded the Teqball Club of Bengaluru to help promote the sport at the grassroots level.A seven-time national champion, she has emerged as one of the trailblazers of Indian Teqball. Earlier in 2026, she finished ninth at the Teqball World Championships in Romania, further strengthening her credentials on the international stage. Her performances at the Asian Games have now given her an opportunity to add a historic medal to her achievements.Quimcy Dsouza’s Asian Games 2026 campaignQuimcy made an impressive start to her Asian Games debut, topping Group A with two wins to secure direct qualification for the women’s singles semifinals.She opened her campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over top-seeded Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto. After losing the first set 10-12, Quimcy fought back to win the second 12-11 before clinching the decider 13-11. She then defeated Cambodia’s Koemyean DY 12-9, 12-7 in straight sets to finish at the top of her group and book a place in the last four.Quimcy falls short in semifinal against IndonesiaQuimcy started her semifinal against Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya on a strong note, winning the opening set 12-7. Sumaya responded in the second, recovering from an early deficit to take it 12-9 and force a decider.The Indian raced to a 3-0 lead in the third set and extended it to 4-1. However, Sumaya mounted a comeback, took control of the decider and won it 12-7 to secure her place in the final. The defeat ended Quimcy’s hopes of reaching the gold-medal match, but she will have another opportunity to finish her debut Asian Games campaign on the podium.Bronze medal match offers chance to make historyQuimcy will face Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto in Sunday’s bronze-medal match. The Indian had defeated Sakamoto in the group stage, but will need to reproduce that performance to secure a place on the podium.A win would earn India its first-ever Teqball medal at the Asian Games. Quimcy has also competed in mixed doubles alongside Mohamed Anas Imran Beg. The Indian pair defeated the Philippines’ Jhoana Abulencia and Prince Agustin in their Group A opener.Teqball, invented in Hungary, combines elements of football and table tennis and is played on a curved table. The sport is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026, with five medal events: men’s and women’s singles, men’s and women’s doubles, and mixed doubles.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why was the Asian Games 2026 flag-hoisting ceremony delayed?
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA: The clock is ticking for Japan, most unusually. A country synonymous with punctuality and quiet efficiency has been struggling with the clock .
articles.body: NAGOYA: The clock is ticking for Japan, most unusually. A country synonymous with punctuality and quiet efficiency has been struggling with the clock in its role as Asian Games host.On Friday, the flag-hoisting ceremony for six contingents — India, Yemen, North Korea, Palestine, Chinese Taipei and Timor-Leste — was delayed by more than an hour because of what organisers described as “miscommunication” between the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) and the Games organising committee (ANAGOC).The ceremony at Garden Pier was scheduled for 1:30 pm local time but was initially pushed back by 20 minutes, following which the ceremonial band began playing. However, just before the contingents were due to take the stage, they were asked not to proceed and were made to wait before eventually being sent back to the waiting area.No Indian athlete was in attendance, but chef de mission Sahdev Yadav and deputy chefs de mission Sharath Kamal, Anjali Bhagwat, Lijo Thottan and Alaknanda Ashok were present.Initially, the delay was attributed to the late arrival of the chief guest. An ANAGOC official later offered a different explanation.“The communication between the Olympic Council of Asia executive board and the organising committee was not well, that’s why this happened. It’s not like somebody delayed the ceremony,” the official said.‘THERE IS MISMANAGEMENT’India’s chef de mission Yadav, meanwhile, sought to assure that efforts were being made to ensure athletes were not inconvenienced by the organisational issues that have plagued the Games in the build-up.“Initially there were problems, but we have booked extra hotel rooms. Our officials are at the airport to sort out issues. There is mismanagement, but in a Games on this scale it happens, but we are focused on solving the problem of our athletes. We have booked about 18 extra hotel rooms and are now looking at 10 more,” Yadav told reporters.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: World champion D Gukesh has offered some context behind Arjun Erigaisi’s shock defeat in the opening round of the Chess Olympiad, saying India’s players had endured a hectic start to the tournament and were left waiting for hours to get their rooms.Arjun, India’s second-ranked player, suffered a surprise defeat against Thailand’s 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap on Board 1. The 23-year-old, playing with the white pieces, had a winning position at different stages but eventually faltered in the endgame.Gukesh said the team’s difficult arrival and accommodation issues had affected the players.“Arjun’s first game was very unfortunate, but also worth mentioning that we had a very hectic travel and then the first day there were some organisation issues,” Gukesh said in an interview with FIDE after his Round 3 win over Italy's Sabino Brunello.“So like Arjun got a room probably a few hours before he went. I mean, we all waited for like six hours to get a room. So obviously the first round Arjun, he was just tired and he blundered in the end.”The world champion added that the situation had improved since the opening day and the players were now better rested.“The first day was a bit tricky for all of us, but after that, I think we are all rested. articles.title: Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0 to shatter Alonso’s London honeymoon
articles.summary: Chelsea left with one point from their last three Premier League games after a 3-0 defeat at neighbours Brentford.
articles.body:
Brentford exposed Chelsea’s defensive problems to inflict a damaging 3-0 defeat that gives Xabi Alonso plenty to ponder during a three-week international break.

After a promising start to life under the former Real Madrid coach, Chelsea have picked up just one point from their last three league games.

Goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fabio Carvalho took unbeaten Brentford above their west London neighbours late on Friday and up to third in the table.

“I have this unbelievable calm around that team because I trust them. It’s nice to see it come to fruition,” said Brentford boss Keith Andrews.

Chelsea had quickly earned the reputation as the Premier League’s great entertainers under Alonso, with their opening four games containing 19 goals.

But the loss of Joao Pedro to a knee injury subdued the Blues’ free-flowing attack as Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers were comfortably kept in check by the Bees.

“At the moment we are not being consistent enough to compete during the whole game,” said Alonso.

“It’s about everything. It’s about the mentality. It’s about football, tactical things that we need to keep improving that we can do much better.”

Alonso said after last weekend’s 2-2 draw against Hull, he was hoping for more “boring” games going forward.

The Spaniard sought control as he made four changes in all, handing Jordan Henderson his first Chelsea start against the 36-year-old’s former club.

Alonso got his wish during a flat first half in which neither goalkeeper was seriously tested, but Brentford were the more threatening side in the second period.

The visitors’ frailty from set-pieces led to the opening goal when Jannick Schuster rose highest to meet Mikkel Damsgaard’s corner, and Anthony was left with a simple task to head into an unguarded net just after the hour mark.

Chelsea’s response was muted, and as they pushed forward in search of an equaliser, Alonso’s men were picked off on the counterattack.

Kevin Schade should have scored the second goal himself when played clean through on Emi Martinez.

But even after the Argentinian goalkeeper spread himself to save, the rebound fell kindly for Thiago to end his goal drought.

The Brazilian netted 25 times last season, earning a shock call-up to Carlo Ancelotti’s World Cup squad as a result.

Thiago has looked shorn of confidence in the early weeks of the campaign and tore off his shirt in celebration after netting for the first time in the Premier League this season.

Chelsea have conceded at least twice in all five league games under Alonso, and there was further punishment to come in stoppage time.

Schade’s low cross was deflected into the path of Carvalho, who fired high past Martinez to leave Andrews yelling into the night sky in delight.

Brentford, who also beat Tottenham 3-0 on the opening weekend of the season, sit behind only defending champions Arsenal and Manchester City at the top of the table.

By contrast, Chelsea were handed another reminder of the gap Alonso must bridge to make them title contenders once more.

articles.title: Celtics Trade Pitch Lands Jamal Murray to Form New Big 3 in Boston
articles.summary: A new Boston Celtics trade idea doing the rounds would see the storied franchise land Denver Nuggets All-Star Jamal Murray. The post Celtics Trade Pitch Land...
articles.body:
Anew Boston Celtics trade idea doing the rounds would see the storied franchise land Denver Nuggets All-Star Jamal Murray , forming a new Big 3 in Beantown alongside Jayson Tatum and Paul George .

Nuggets would receive: Derrick White , Sam Hauser

The clean 2-for-1 trade does not include any picks or additional salary fillers, making it a very feasible scenario for both the Nuggets and Celtics.

Are the Celtics really ready to trust Derrick White's shot again? Last year, the All-Defensive guard hit a shooting slump he couldn't recover from.

After shooting a league-low 32% among players taking at least 8.0 threes per game, he stunk it up even more in the playoffs, converting on a brutal 27% from beyond the arc. Many felt White's inability to make open shots was a big reason why the Celtics blew a 3-1 series lead to the Philadelphia 76ers in the playoffs.

This hypothetical Celtics trade idea comes with its fair share of risks. Joe Mazzulla's team will struggle to replace White's intangibles and defensive IQ. However, Jamal Muray's elite shotmaking and playmaking could help soften the blow.

A starting five of Murray, Payton Pritchard , Paul George, Jayson Tatum and Mitchell Robinson (or Neemias Queta ) can put together an elite offense for Mazzulla. And the defense should still be serviceable, given that George and Tatum still rate as good perimeter stoppers and Prichard is a pest who fights through every ball screen.

Also worth noting is that Murray is signed through 2028-29 , giving the C's at least a two-year window with the Big 3 of Tatum, George and Murray, and an extended window with the pairing of Tatum and Murray. It could led to Banner No. 19.

Jamal Murray isn't the worst defensive guard in the league (he's no Trae Young ), but the Toronto native got exposed and picked on by the Minnesota Timberwolves in the playoffs this year. So much so that Timberwolves wing Jaden McDaniels called out Murray as a "bad defender" while revealing that his team's game plan was to relentlessly pick apart and target the Nuggets guard.

One wonders if the Nuggets will run into similar issues next year if they keep their starting backcourt of Murray and Christian Braun . There's a reason they have been unable to get past the second round of the postseason since their 2023 title run.

Derrick White is the sort of culture-changing guard who can almost singlehandedly transform Denver's defense. A starting five of White, Braun (or Hauser), Cameron Johnson , Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic projects as a much better defensive unit. Furthermore, White — who had a down year as a three-point shooter last season — could regain his touch playing off of Jokic's phenomenal playmaking. After all, the three-time MVP has an uncanny knack of finding open shooters.

articles.title: It's official, Liverpool have their new Roberto Firmino and he's incredible
articles.summary: There's a new Roberto Firmino on the scene at Anfield.The Brazilian remains one of the most underappreciated club icons of recent memory.Roberto Firmino neve...
articles.body:
There's a new Roberto Firmino on the scene at Anfield.

The Brazilian remains one of the most underappreciated club icons of recent memory.

Roberto Firmino never seemed interested in chasing the spotlight or soaking up the acclaim of the Anfield crowd. Instead, he was the perfect cog in Jurgen Klopp's machine, quietly keeping everything ticking while providing the energy and intelligence that allowed Sadio Mane and Mo Salah to flourish.

Firmino was incredibly selfless, always willing to sacrifice his own numbers for the benefit of the team. But that shouldn't disguise just how talented he was. He could produce moments of genuine brilliance while relentlessly pressing, linking play and creating space for others.

Without Firmino, it is difficult to imagine Liverpool achieving everything they did under Klopp. His contribution was enormous, even if it was sometimes overlooked.

Liverpool's Roberto Firmino hole and the plans to fix it

Since Firmino left, Liverpool have struggled to find a genuine replacement. Darwin Nunez brought plenty of energy and hard work, but he never quite possessed the Brazilian's finesse or ability to link everything together.

However, the Reds have now moved on and embraced a different philosophy. Their new No.9 does not necessarily need to facilitate for everyone else. Instead, Liverpool want a forward in the mould of Sadio Mane and Mo Salah - someone whose first instinct is to score.

Alexander Isak fits that profile perfectly. The Swede represents Liverpool's future and he was signed to put the ball in the net. So far, he has delivered, scoring three goals in his first three Premier League games under Andoni Iraola .

But behind him, another player is emerging as Liverpool's new Firmino.

Ever since pre-season, the Welshman has emerged as a genuine option in the attacking line. Koumas scored against Sunderland in Iraola's first ever game, and he's been regularly making cameos in competitive matches as well.

Koumas made his Premier League and Champions League debut under Iraola, and it's clear he is a key part of the Spaniard's plans.

It's easy to see why, Koumas presses tirelessly. Like Firmino he works for the team, and he facilitates and makes everyone better around him.

His most recent performance against Tottenham may not have seen him score a goal nor get an assist yet he was still awarded with the Man of the Match award.

That's because he worked so hard for the team and his press was so good. It reminded us of watching prime Firmino.

Koumas is still young. He's only 20-years-old. At the same age Firmino was just starting out at Hoffenheim . Under Iraola, the Welshman could genuinely become a huge asset, and in the process the Reds have found their new Firmino.

The game against Tottenham on Tuesday night made it official.

articles.title: Arizona volleyball finds winning combination in reverse sweep of San Diego State
articles.summary: It felt like déjà vu. A day after dropping three straight sets to San Diego in a very uninspiring fashion, Arizona volleyball was in a two-set hole to San Di...
articles.body:
It felt like déjà vu. A day after dropping three straight sets to San Diego in a very uninspiring fashion, Arizona volleyball was in a two-set hole to San Diego State. Just like the day before, the Wildcats had yet to reach 20 points in a set. Then, they found something that worked.

Arizona came back to take a 3-2 (16-25, 19-25, 25-18, 25-19, 15-8) victory in the Aztecs' home opener.

"I love the fact that we fought together and we played together the entire time," said Arizona head coach Rita Stubbs . "To me, that's always the most important part. And I kept telling us, like, win or lose, it doesn't matter. It's one point at a time. Stay together. Play to win. Be aggressive. Pick your line, and have purposeful communication, because sometimes we talk and no one's really listening."

It took a lot of experimenting and adjustments. Stubbs made multiple lineup changes. She made tactical changes. Eventually, it all came together.

Arizona was out-blocked by San Diego on Thursday night. The blocking was again a problem on Friday in the early going.

San Diego State was able to get just enough of the Wildcats' fingertips to score points on balls that were headed out. Arizona wasn't stuff blocking and it wasn't even slowing the ball down for the defense; it was simply getting enough contact to rack up points for the opposition.

"We made a few adjustments with the block to help that out, and they were coachable and they listened," Stubbs said. "So, super excited!"

Those changes made a huge difference. The Wildcats ended with 13 total blocks after getting just one in the first two sets combined. Senior middle blocker Journey Tucker led the way for both teams with eight total blocks, including two solo.

Tucker was also a big part of the Arizona offense. She tied right side Kennedy Osunsanmi and reserve outside hitter Hayden Reeder with eight kills, trailing only right side Renee Jones for the team high. Tucker led the match with a .571 hitting percentage.

"It was nice to see Journey stepped up," Stubbs said. "She was really aggressive, as well."

Jones was once again a big part of the story. The sophomore went into the season chasing Osunsanmi and Britt Carlson for playing time in Arizona's 6-2 system. When Carlson went down with an injury before the season opener, Jones stepped in.

She contributes 1.89 kills per set this season while splitting time with Osunsanmi on the right side. That comes in third on the team behind Destiny Ndam-Simpson and Osunsanmi. Her .311 hitting percentage is second behind Tucker among players with at least 50 attacks. Her 0.76 blocks per set are third on the team among players who have played at least 25 sets and first among Arizona's pin hitters. Her five solo blocks tie Tucker for the team high.

On Friday, Jones had 11 kills on .375 hitting. Her five total blocks were second on the team. She contributed 13.5 points and four digs. She was the only Wildcat to hit double digits in kills.

Reeder has begun getting more playing time of late largely because she's Arizona's second-best passer on the left side. With Ndam-Simpson struggling on both attacking and serve receive, Reeder came in during the second set. She started the final three sets.

The lanky freshman had eight kills. She received a match high 34 serves with only two receiving errors. Her 34 receptions were twice as many as any other Wildcat. She also had four total blocks, including one solo. Her total blocks tied fellow freshman Marina Vosloo for third on the team.

"Hayden, what she went in and did—and the energy she provided—was instrumental," Stubbs said.

With Arizona searching for something that worked, Stubbs substituted regularly. Only four players started every set, including freshman libero Gigi Whann . Only six players appeared in every set. Those included Harmony Sample , who is the second setter in the 6-2 system, and Jones, who is the second opposite in that system. Payton Woods started the second set as the other opposite before Osunsanmi returned in the third.

Whann was the third freshman to make an important contribution for Arizona.

"I think it's important because they need to know that working hard has its benefits," Stubbs said. "Typically, there could be a set line up, and it's like you work hard the entire time and never get a reward after it. It becomes a little discouraging at some point, and that's never the intent but let's be honest, that's exactly what happens. So the fact that they kept grinding and they say they don't care and they just go get it done the best way they can is exactly what you would want."

San Diego State played a very clean match for the first two sets. They had 19 kills in each of those frames. They hit an efficient .395 in the first and .371 in the second.

The final three sets looked like a completely different team. The Aztecs had more hitting errors than kills in both the fourth and fifth. In the third, they had 14 kills but gave almost all of those points away with 12 hitting errors. After hitting .383 combined in the sets they won, they cratered to -.038 over the final three sets.

A big part of the waning efficiency on SDSU's side of the net was improved serving by Arizona. The Wildcats had all five of their aces in the third and fourth sets.

They also began to go on longer service runs. Vosloo, Carlie Cisneros , and both of Arizona's setters had at least one significant service run in the last three sets.

Cisneros served 15 times in over the final three sets, leading the way for the Wildcats. Vosloo served a total of 13 points during Arizona's three winning sets after serving just three times in the second set.

The win will make the Wildcats' bus trip back from San Diego more pleasant than it might have been. They will finish their nonconference schedule on Tuesday when they take another bus ride to El Paso, Tex. to face UTEP. A win against the Miners would put them at 5-6 in nonconference play heading into next week's Big 12 opener.

articles.title: Houston comes up inches short against Texas Tech but sends a message in loss. Cougars are contenders
articles.summary: Conner Weigman's stretch for a two-point conversion came up inches short in a 28-26 loss to Tech but Cougars showed they are Big 12 contenders.
articles.body:
LUBBOCK - If the University of Houston wants to know just how close it is to being a contender in the Big 12, well, the answer can be measured in inches.

Conner Weigman 's desperation lunge for the goal line on a two-point conversion with 49 seconds came up short as the No. 22 Cougars lost to No. 13 Texas Tech 28-26 at Galaxy Stadium.

"There are no moral victories," UH coach Willie Fritz said after the Cougars (2-1) lost in the Big 12 opener. "We came here to win, and we didn't win."

No, but the Cougars gave the defending Big 12 champions all they could handle. UH put together a dominant start, taking a 10-0 lead and controlling the clock for nearly 13 minutes in the first quarter. UH led 17-14 at halftime on a 46-yard over-the-shoulder catch by Koby Young.

And down 28-20 with about three minutes left, Weigman marched the Cougars 10 plays and 88 yards, capped off by a 10-yard touchdown catch by tight end Patrick Overmyer.

A chance to send an early-season message to the rest of college football.

Weigman dropped back to pass, couldn't find an open receiver and took off to the left side. He was wrapped up by Texas Tech linebacker Austin Romaine at the 3-yard line. His knee was down - video review confirmed - before he lunged forward to extend the ball across the goal line.

"They played it well," said Weigman, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. "I was trying to make something happen. I feel like some of our guys were covered. I tried to buy some time. You have to reach and try and get the two-point conversion. I have it all I've got."

Fritz said he saw the replay on the stadium video board.

"Hard to tell," he said. "We thought there was a chance his knee had not touched when he extended, but they didn't see it that way."

"I felt like it was close," Weigman added.

In between a dominant first-quarter and a wild finish, the Cougars did just enough to cost themselves what would have been the program's biggest win since beating third-ranked Louisville and Heisman Trophy winner Lamar Jackson in 2016.

Two drives inside the red zone stalled, forcing the Cougars to settle for 31- and 28-yard field goals by Jonathan Dimas. One particularly damning sequence came late in the third quarter with the Cougars at the Tech 4-yard line. On fourth-and-2, UH right guard McKenzie Agnello was called for a false start.

"A big part of this game is who scores touchdowns instead of kicking field goals," Fritz said. "It's hard to get down there, and when you get down there, you want to maximize it and score touchdowns. We just didn't do that on a couple of occasions."

Fritz said the Cougars struggled against the run late in the game, allowing a 29-yard touchdown run on the first drive of the second half and a 1-yard run by Cameron Dickey for the eventual game-winner with 7½ minutes left in the game.

There also were some misses on "some fairly easy tackles" on pass plays late in the game. The Cougars managed interceptions by cornerbacks Jalen Mayo and Will James, but gave up six pass plays of at least 20 yards.

"When you play a close ball game like that, you have to play close to error-free, and we did not," Fritz said. He added: "We played OK, but not our best."

It was almost enough to pull off one of the biggest upsets of the season's first month.

Texas Tech, led by a defense that features six NFL draft picks, was never really challenged last season, winning all 12 regular-season games by at least 22 points.

This is not the same Red Raiders, who showed flaws throughout Friday's game when backup quarterback Thomas Castellanos threw an interception on the Red Raiders' first offensive play. Texas Tech managed only 30 yards in the first quarter - 28 coming on a catch by Kenny Johnson.

After Amare Thomas' 11-yard touchdown catch gave the Cougars a 10-0 lead, Tech recovered on a 35-yard TD catch by Johnson and a 3-yard run by Castellanos.

"We've got to have that intensity the whole game," Mayo said. "We can't have it the first half and then shut it down in the second half's it has to be all four quarters."

In a dark area just outside the locker room, the Cougars gathered for a few words.

"It's over with," Mayo said. "There's nothing we can do about it now until the next time we see them."

Could that be a rematch in the Big 12 championship game?

"We're going to see them again," Mayo said.

articles.title: Lions’ Week 2 Loss Sparks Intriguing Trade Idea for Raiders’ Maxx Crosby
articles.summary: Until the trade deadline comes and goes, the trade speculation regarding the Las Vegas Raiders‘ Maxx Crosby won’t quiet down. While Crosby appears happy with...
articles.body:
Until the trade deadline comes and goes, the trade speculation regarding the Las Vegas Raiders ' Maxx Crosby won't quiet down. While Crosby appears happy with the Silver and Black, that doesn't mean the Raiders won't get calls leading up to the trade deadline on Nov. 10.

Moreover, Crosby showed in Week 1 that he's his usual disruptive self, and even Las Vegas is taking steps like putting him on a snap count to ensure the veteran edge rusher can play well not just this season, but well into his 30s.

Despite the Raiders putting Crosby on a slight load management plan, the veteran edge rusher was still impactful, earning a 90.5 PFF grade in the win against Miami . Moreover, he recorded eight pressures, two sacks, one QB hit, and five hurries.

With Crosby showing he's performing at a level many expect, Zachary Rotman of FanSided floated a trade idea in a Sept. 18 article that would send Crosby to the Detroit Lions , who are coming off a Week 2 loss and desperately need help on defense if they want to be a playoff team this season.

In his trade idea, Rotman has Crosby heading to Detroit in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick. The Raiders initially got two first-round picks when they traded Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens this past offseason.

Lions Urged to Take Risk With Trading Two First Rounders

Trading two first-round picks is always risky for any team, but with the Lions trying to win now and having key players in their prime years, it might be a risk that they'll need to take.

"Admittedly, the odds of a Maxx Crosby trade are probably slim, but the Las Vegas Raiders did agree to trade him over the summer, and they could very well do so again if the right deal presented itself," Rotman wrote in his Sept. 18 article.

"Well, what about basically the exact same deal as the one that didn't get completed? It'd be a risk for the Lions to part with a pair of first-round selections in exchange for a player who failed a physical with the Ravens, but Crosby certainly looked healthy when he recorded 1.5 sacks in Week 1."

Raiders Managing Maxx Crosby's Work Load

The question with Crosby is how he'll age, since after this season he'll be in his 30s. At least for the Raiders' sake, they are looking to protect and keep Crosby fresh. ESPN Raiders writer Ryan McFadden said he wasn't caught off guard that the team took this load management approach with the 29-year-old.

"It looks like a sign of load management, and this is something that's not surprising," McFadden said on the Sept. 15 edition of "Raiders Collective." "You're talking about your top defensive player. He's 29 years old, coming off an offseason knee procedure. He's had multiple surgeries in the past, and to me, this is about preserving his career and making sure you're able to get him playing at a high level for the duration of his contract.

"So that's why I'm not shocked about Klint Kubiak's call to rest him for that extended period of time. When you go back to the league meetings, general manager John Spytek said they were going to have conversations with Crosby about potentially managing his snap count because of that. Because you kind of want to let him have longevity."

articles.summary: Lamine Camara Transfer Latest as Monaco Leave January Window OpenLamine Camara has emerged once again as a serious name to watch ahead of the January transfe...
articles.body:
Lamine Camara Transfer Latest as Monaco Leave January Window Open

Lamine Camara has emerged once again as a serious name to watch ahead of the January transfer window, with Standard reporting that Monaco could yet be forced into a decision on the Senegal midfielder.

Chelsea came close to landing Camara in the previous window, with a £47m agreement understood to have been reached before Monaco abruptly halted the move. The proposed switch would have seen the player sign a six-year contract, with the option of a further year, only for the French side to reverse course late in the process.

Liverpool have also been credited with interest and Monaco chief executive Thiago Scuro has now offered insight that keeps the situation alive. His remarks suggest the Ligue 1 club would prefer to retain Camara for the remainder of the season, but that outcome may depend heavily on other outgoing business.

Monaco transfer plan shapes Lamine Camara future

Scuro explained Monaco's stance clearly when discussing their winter strategy. "The original plan is to find a solution for Balogun . If we find that, it will give Monaco the opportunity to keep Lamine and Golovin until the end of the season," Scuro told RMC Sport.

He continued, "That is the ideal plan, but we can't control the decisions and what will happen in the winter." Those comments are significant. They do not place Camara firmly on the market, but they do acknowledge that circumstances could change quickly if Monaco fail to move Folarin Balogun on or if a compelling offer arrives.

Liverpool interest remains worth monitoring

For Liverpool, this feels like a situation to monitor rather than one accelerating towards an immediate conclusion. Camara is highly regarded, energetic, technically polished and capable of developing further at the top level. If Monaco are left needing a sale, his profile and the previously agreed £47m figure make him one of the more attractive midfield options likely to become available.

The player himself has struck a calm tone since the collapse of his Chelsea move. "There was a possibility I could leave," Camara explained. "It didn't go through at the last minute and that's part of football. I've turned the page and am focusing on the season.

"I can help the team a lot. Football moves fast. Maybe other opportunities will come along. But for now, I'm staying focused on the season with Monaco." That leaves the door open, and for Liverpool, that alone is enough to keep attention fixed on this developing Monaco transfer story.

From a Liverpool perspective, this is the sort of report that naturally sparks interest. Camara looks like a player with the mobility, intensity and composure to thrive in a high-level midfield, and if Monaco are genuinely vulnerable to the right January offer, Liverpool should be paying very close attention.

There is always a degree of caution needed with winter business, especially when clubs can be pushed into reactive decisions rather than well-planned ones. Even so, a £47m valuation for a player of Camara's age and upside feels like the kind of market opportunity that can become very attractive very quickly.

What will matter most is whether Liverpool view him as a strong stylistic fit for Andoni Iraola 's next phase. If the recruitment team believe he can add legs, aggression and technical security, this could be one to pursue seriously. Supporters will always dream when a talented young midfielder becomes available, and this feels more credible than idle gossip.

The most encouraging part of the report is that Monaco are not speaking in absolutes. They have a preferred plan, but they are also admitting that events may dictate something else. That is exactly the type of scenario top clubs try to exploit. If the opportunity opens in January, Liverpool should be ready.

articles.title: Every word an emotional Holger Rune said after winning his first match since rupturing his Achilles 335 days ago
articles.summary: Holger Rune has made a triumphant return to competition after nearly a year out of action. Rune ruptured his left Achilles tendon during a match...
articles.body:
Holger Rune has made a triumphant return to competition after nearly a year out of action.

Rune ruptured his left Achilles tendon during a match in Stockholm last year, and as a result has been kept out of action ever since.

Despite attempts to make his comeback ever since the clay court season, Rune has been forced to miss all four Grand Slams this year.

Rune has now officially made his comeback at home in Denmark for the Davis Cup tie against Bulgaria in Hillerød, and he was clearly emotional following his 6-3, 6-3 win over Iliyan Radulov.

Holger Rune admits it has been 'pretty brutal' for him in injury comeback

Former world number four Rune, who is now the world number 144, spoke in the on-court interview after winning his first match since rupturing his Achilles 335 days ago.

When asked how he was feeling, Rune simply said, "Wow it's crazy," before being caught up in the emotion of it all and taking a step back.

After recomposing himself, Rune then explained how difficult the comeback has been for him, describing it as the 'perfect way' for him to make his comeback.

"It's been, it's been pretty brutal," admitted Rune. "Obviously a super unfortunate injury that happened 11 months ago, but we have trained a whole lot. I've gotten up every day and done my rehab to be able to stand here today.

"So I'm proud of myself, and this is the perfect way for me to start here in Denmark, in front of the best crowd in the world. So thank you so much for coming out and supporting."

Holger Rune will now face Grigor Dimitrov in crucial Davis Cup match

Rune is only just getting started in Denmark's tie against Bulgaria, as he now has an important part to play, with a singles rubber against Grigor Dimitrov now looming.

With the tie set at 1-1, it is set to be a tense second day of the tie, where the outcome will be decided, following a doubles match and the potential for two more singles rubbers.

It also means that Rune knows he can still have a say in the outcome when he takes on Dimitrov in the fourth rubber of the tie. This will be a fifth meeting between Rune and Dimitrov, with their head-to-head currently level at two wins apiece.

Rune beat Dimitrov, 3-6 7-6(6) 7-6(4) 6-3

This was a very positive start for Rune, who has already confirmed his upcoming plans for the coming weeks.

After representing Denmark in the Davis Cup, Rune is scheduled to make his ATP Tour return at the Japan Open, before competing at the Shanghai Masters.

articles.title: Celtic vs Rangers preview: Gers chase back-to-back wins against arch-rivals
articles.summary: Celtic and Rangers meet for the second time in seven days on Sunday, but the setting and stakes will be very different when the Old Firm rivals clash at Celt...
articles.body:
Celtic and Rangers meet for the second time in seven days on Sunday, but the setting and stakes will be very different when the Old Firm rivals clash at Celtic Park in the Scottish Premiership.

Rangers produced one of their best performances of the season last weekend, beating Celtic 3-0 at Ibrox in the League Cup quarter-finals

The Gers now have the chance to follow that up with another victory over their biggest rivals. Unfortunately, the numbers suggest that will be a difficult task.

Celtic have won all six of their Premiership matches this season and sit five points clear of Rangers at the top of the table.

The champions have also lost just two of their last 12 home meetings with Rangers across all competitions.

However, recent head-to-head history also shows that this fixture has become increasingly unpredictable.

Last Sunday's 3-0 victory was Rangers' second win over Celtic in their last six meetings, while they have now avoided defeat in seven of the previous 10 encounters.

The Gers also won 3-1 at Celtic Park in January. Their wider league form has also improved significantly.

Rangers failed to win either of their opening two Premiership matches, drawing with Dundee United before losing 1-0 to Hibernian.

Since then, they have won four consecutive league games against Aberdeen, Falkirk, Motherwell and St Mirren.

Rangers have now won seven of their last eight matches in all competitions, with their only defeat coming against Jablonec.

Besides local bragging rights, victory on Sunday would cut Celtic's five-point advantage at the top of the Premiership.

Celtic have been considerably more consistent domestically.

Their six league victories have produced 14 goals, while they have conceded just three.

They are also unbeaten in their last 13 Premiership matches, stretching back to March.

However, that impressive run has not carried into their most recent results.

Celtic have lost their last two matches, falling 3-0 to Rangers before suffering a 3-1 Europa League defeat against Ferencvaros.

Their home record against Rangers nevertheless remains a major factor.

Celtic have won six of their last eight league meetings with Rangers at Celtic Park, with one draw and one defeat in the other two games.

Rangers remain without Lawrence Shankland because of a hamstring injury, while Youssef Chermiti is ruled out with a cruciate ligament problem.

Kevin Kelsy is expected to lead the line again after scoring against Celtic last weekend, with Rangers potentially naming an unchanged XI.

Celtic are without Alistair Johnston , Callum Osmand and Jota , while Yang Hyun-Jun is away with South Korea at the Asian Games.

Benjamin Nygren and Kasper Hogh are among those expected to come into O'Neill's starting XI after the midweek defeat.

articles.title: Texas Tech football news: Joey McGuire calls out reporters who picked Houston over Red Raiders
articles.summary: Joey McGuire did not wait for a question. Moments after No. 13 Texas Tech held off No. 22 Houston 28-26 in Friday night’s Big 12 opener at Galaxy Stadium, th...
articles.body:
Joey McGuire did not wait for a question. Moments after No. 13 Texas Tech held off No. 22 Houston 28-26 in Friday night's Big 12 opener at Galaxy Stadium, the Red Raiders coach stepped to the podium and started handing out sarcastic thank-yous.

"A couple guys I'd like to thank before we get into questions. I'd like to thank Josh Pate," McGuire told reporters after the game . "Keep it up, Pate. He's my buddy and everything, but keep picking against us, man. I appreciate that. You say that he's watched us the last couple weeks, so we don't look the same. We don't look the same, but we're 3-0."

He was not finished. McGuire also took aim at Rick Neuheisel and the CBS Sports crew who had gone against Texas Tech. "Coach Neuheisel, you started off on your crew, with your old crew, picking against us, man. I appreciate that," he said. "That just adds fire to it, and man, just keep picking against us. We love that stuff. We love being doubted."

The game gave both sides plenty to argue about. Houston led 17-14 just before halftime after Koby Young hauled in a 46-yard touchdown, making an over-the-shoulder catch and pinning the ball against his shoulder pads while falling over the pylon. Will Hammond had earlier connected with Kenny Johnson on a 35-yard score a minute into the second quarter.

Texas Tech seized control after the break. J'Koby Williams, who managed just five yards on two carries in the first half, ripped off runs of 19, 5 and 29 yards, the last of which put the Red Raiders ahead 21-17 two and a half minutes into the third quarter. Cameron Dickey added a one-yard touchdown run with 7:36 remaining, and Tech stopped a late two-point conversion to preserve the margin.

Conner Weigman finished 27-of-38 for 282 yards in the loss. Texas Tech has now beaten Houston eight straight times.

"It just shows the resilience of this team and the belief they have in each other," McGuire said. "There was never a time that those guys got down."

articles.title: Chelsea vs. Birmingham, Women’s Super League: Preview, team news, how to watch
articles.summary: Can we keep going?
articles.body:
An astonishing 5-0 win away against Manchester United was exactly what Chelsea Women needed after a Women's Super League season debut that left a bad impression on everybody. To show this wasn't mere happenstance the Blues host recently promoted outfit Birmingham City at Stamford Bridge, hoping they don't fall into the trappings that caught them a couple of weeks ago at the same stage.

Date / Time: Saturday, September 19, 2026, 12.45 BST; 7:45am EDT Venue: Stamford Bridge, SW6 Referee: Alice Parker

On TV: Sky Sports Premier League (UK); none (USA); elsewhere Streaming: Sky Go (UK); Paramount+ (USA)

Chelsea team news: The Blues' victory over Manchester United last weekend reminded us of times not too long ago when we easily dispatched any team that wasn't in the top three of the league. Of course we were greatly helped by a Red Devils side that looked completely clueless as we relentlessly pressed them. This shouldn't take merit away from the pressing work itself, which was a sight to behold and gave many a feeling they haven't felt in a while when watching this team under head coach Sonia Bompastor.

Injuries, which haven't helped Sonia in the slightest, continue to be a concern. We will have centre-backs Nathalie Björn and Naomi Girma back in contention, as well as centre-forward Melvine Malard . However Mayra Ramírez, Manaka Matsukubo and Erin Cuthbert remain sidelined.

Birmingham City team news: The West Midlands club returned to the Women's Super League after a four-season stretch by winning the Women's Super League 2 on goal difference – +22 versus +18 GD as they were tied at 44 points with Crystal Palace .

They made some investments into the team as they don't want to return to the WSL 2 anytime soon. Manchester United veterans, Millie Turner and Lisa Naalsund, joined the club. And so did goalkeeper Sophie Baggaley , in a return to her former youth team.

After losing their WSL debut 3-1 away to defending champions Manchester City and letting a 2-0 lead slip to a 2-2 draw to Brighton at home, they will seek to at least surprise the Blues much like Aston Villa did at the Bridge.
